solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copies sent around, including one in colour

indicators.note: sending something around turns it to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
to include is to take in, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to ape is to copy, so 'copies' is the verb apes
I = one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Photocopies being circulated, one of them printed in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copies' reads as a plural noun, but it is the verb: to ape someone is to copy them. APES turned round gives SEPA, and the one goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tint, originally an ink made from cuttlefish, used in old photographs.

clue.text: Place prints automated slips

indicators.note: a thing that slips loses its footing and its shape, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder, the whole length of the grid

explanation.surface: An office where the printer spits out paper by itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is a British way of saying home ('back to my place'), and it is all the definition there is. 'Slips' looks like paper slips from the printer, and is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat is somewhere a person lives, and in British speech a home is often called someone's place.

clue.text: Carefully arrange pawns, maintaining edge

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the outer piece keeps the other within it

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for pawn, doubled for the plural
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A chess player fussily setting out the pawns, keeping them along the side of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'arrange pawns' look like one phrase; the definition stops after 'arrange'. Two P's for pawns sit either side of the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to fuss over appearance, adjusting hair or clothes with great care and attention to detail.

clue.text: Poisonous plant — one chokes on it

indicators.note: something that chokes has a thing stuck in its throat, so one piece lodges within another

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
the two words taken as they stand

explanation.surface: A warning: the plant is so toxic that anyone who eats it chokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a person, and it is ACE, which has ON IT stuck in its throat. 'On it' is used word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a garden flower whose roots and leaves are deadly toxic.

clue.text: Via text: See you after party — quick drink and a show of some sort?

indicators.note: one thing written after another sits to its right in an across answer

blocks.note: a do is a party
text-message shorthand for 'see you'
a dram is a small drink of whisky
used as it stands, and also the first word of the definition

explanation.surface: A text message: see you after the party, for a quick drink and some kind of performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' at the end does double duty: it is the last letter of the answer and the start of the definition, which is why the definition ends in a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a television programme dramatising real events, one particular genre of broadcast programme.

clue.text: Foolish millions taken in by label

indicators.note: what is taken in by something ends up inside it

blocks.note: to dub is to give a name or label
M = million(s)

explanation.surface: Millions of people fooled by a brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Label' looks like a noun, a brand, but it is the verb: to dub is to label. The M for millions goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech dumb means stupid or silly, a common American sense now widespread in Britain too.

clue.text: After outburst, got lifted into pushchair — that needs deciphering

indicators.note: what comes after follows on, placed lower down in a down answer
in a down answer, lifting a word turns it to read from the bottom up
to go into something is to end up inside it

blocks.note: a cry is an outburst
used as it stands
a pram is a baby carriage, near enough a pushchair

explanation.surface: A toddler has a tantrum and gets lifted into the pushchair, a moment that takes some interpreting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a relative clause, 'that needs deciphering', standing for a thing needing decoding. A pram is the British word for a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a text written in code or cipher, so reading it means cracking the cipher first.

clue.text: Follow trainer’s lead and go off for gentle jog

indicators.note: the lead is the front runner, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
the first letter of trainer
food that goes off rots

explanation.surface: Taking the coach's lead and setting off on an easy run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' plays on dog training too, since a lead is a dog's leash; here it means the first letter. 'Go off' in the sense of food spoiling is ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is an easy steady trotting pace, like the unhurried gait of a dog on the move.

clue.text: One of the greats from ten included in a list — wine from the south

indicators.note: what is included in something is placed inside it
read from the south in a down answer, a word runs bottom to top

blocks.note: used as it stands
a ship that lists leans over
X is ten in Roman numerals
red is a wine

explanation.surface: Picking a wine from the southern regions, the tenth item on a wine list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a written list, but it is the verb to lean, as a ship does. 'One of the greats' is a king known by the title 'the Great'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, the Macedonian king who conquered an empire, is one of several rulers given that epithet.

clue.text: Mashed potato father had in an instant

annotation.answer: AT THE DROP OF A HAT

indicators.note: mashing crushes things out of their original form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Dad polished off his mashed potato in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashed potato' reads as one dish, and the first word is the anagram instruction. The definition sits at the end and says how fast the meal went.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediately and without hesitation, from a dropped hat once used as a starting signal.

clue.text: Flour in my pants, regularly

indicators.note: in British slang pants means rubbish or messed up, so the letters are in a bad state

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A baker's complaint that flour keeps getting into their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for rubbish or bad, and in Britain the word also means underwear rather than trousers, which is the picture the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something uniformly means doing it in the same even manner throughout, without variation.

clue.text: Champion’s golf equipment initially hidden in grass

indicators.note: what comes initially comes at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
a thing hidden in another is tucked away within it

blocks.note: G is golf in the radio alphabet
the first letter of equipment
to grass is to inform on someone, and so is to rat

explanation.surface: A champion golfer's kit lies concealed in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer, as is RAT; the golf surface makes it look like turf. 'Champion' is the informal adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British praise: calling something champion or great says it is excellent.

clue.text: Spoil married couple on island

indicators.note: one thing placed on another follows it in an across answer

blocks.note: I = island
M = married
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Pampering newlyweds on their island honeymoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' reads as indulge in the honeymoon picture, and is the other sense, damage. The island comes first because the couple sits on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it, which is what spoiling does to a thing.

clue.text: Use observatory in Arizona — small object briefly comes around

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter
to come around something is to surround it on both sides

blocks.note: S = small
a target is an object or aim, here without its last letter
AZ is the US postal code for Arizona

explanation.surface: Visiting an Arizona observatory while some small object passes by overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Arizona does house famous observatories, so the surface is realistic. 'Object' is an aim or goal, a target, not a thing in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking through a telescope at night is precisely how one studies the stars and planets.

clue.text: Ship has coil fitted to disruptive transmitter

indicators.note: a part fitted to another is joined on beside it

blocks.note: to coil a rope is to wind it
a jammer broadcasts noise to block radio signals

explanation.surface: A vessel's radio has an interfering coil wired into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coil' looks like a noun, an electrical part, in the radio picture; it is the verb to wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A windjammer is a large sailing vessel of the late nineteenth century, a merchant square-rigger.

clue.text: Stripped naked in canvas shelter, finding arousal

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: an awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a doorway or window
NAKED stripped of its outer letters N and D

explanation.surface: A naughty scene of undressing under a tent flap, and the excitement that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers 'arousal' toward sex; the answer is the plainer sense of rousing, waking up. 'Stripped naked' is a natural phrase that hides the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse someone is literally to wake them, so an arousal is a coming out of sleep.

clue.text: Visiting family, dust regularly found inside property

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second one
what is found inside something is enclosed by it

blocks.note: visiting a place is being at it
a tribe is a family or clan
the second and fourth letters of dust

explanation.surface: Visiting relatives and finding dust all over their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' reads as a house in the domestic surface, and is the other sense, a quality something has.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic or quality, which is what a property is in the philosophical or scientific sense.

clue.text: Worst is over — Duke’s protected in former royal house

indicators.note: a thing turned over is flipped, so the word reads backwards
something protected in another is sheltered inside it

blocks.note: to worst an opponent is to defeat them, to rout them
D is the standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Relief that the danger has passed now that the duke is safe in an old palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst is over' reads as a stock phrase, but 'worst' is the verb meaning defeat, and 'is over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English ruling dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I, ending in 1603.

clue.text: Player works endlessly

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters go

blocks.note: works in the sense of a factory, with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A performer who never stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' is a plural-looking singular: a works is a factory. Trimmed at both ends, FACTORY gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is an old word for a stage performer, as in Shakespeare's 'all the men and women merely players'.

clue.text: Concerns after leader leaves eastern capital

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and once it leaves the word starts one later

blocks.note: worries are troubles, here without the opening letter

explanation.surface: Worries in a capital city in the east after its leader departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern capital' wants to be a city such as Moscow; capital here is money, and the money is Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency of Russia, and capital in the sense of funds or money means cash here.

clue.text: Tread path going around unsafe building, perhaps

indicators.note: letters that go around are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Keeping to the path that skirts a dangerous structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: an unsafe building is one kind of the answer, not the only kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is any place or vehicle so dangerous it could kill; a crumbling structure is one instance.

clue.text: She holds craft on course, finally arriving at buoy

indicators.note: what comes finally comes last, so only the closing letter is kept
in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it
to hold something is to have it within your grasp

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird, so a she
craft is skill, art
the last letter of course

explanation.surface: A woman steering a boat on its course, reaching the marker buoy at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' and 'buoy' are both sailing words here; craft is skill, ART, and buoy is the verb, as in buoy up.
explanation.definitionFit: To buoy someone up is to lift their spirits, which is what encouraging or cheering them does.

clue.text: Turning point in hearing — such as this?

definitions.text: Turning point in hearing — such as this?

indicators.note: a word turning round faces the other way, so it reads backwards
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the nub is the central point of a matter
a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A decisive moment in a legal case, and a question about what sort of case it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning point' is a stock phrase, but it splits into the reversal instruction and the point itself. The whole clue then describes the answer: a hearing where things can turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that hears disputes and judges them, such as an employment panel, so it holds hearings.

clue.text: Receding part of cliff is sampled for geological formation

indicators.note: only a part of the words is taken, a run of letters within them
something receding goes backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the run of letters across the ends of these three words

explanation.surface: Samples taken from an eroding cliff face to study the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The geology surface fits the answer exactly, and 'receding' reads as the cliff wearing away rather than as an instruction to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, such as the Massif Central in France.

clue.text: Nurse holds end of mesh over cut

indicators.note: only the end of the word is kept, its closing letter
to hold something is to keep it within your grasp

blocks.note: SRN stands for State Registered Nurse, an old British nursing qualification
the last letter of mesh
O = over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

explanation.surface: A nurse holding a dressing over a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: SRN, State Registered Nurse, was the British nursing grade; setters still use it. 'Over' is O from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn is the past participle of shear, describing hair or wool that has been clipped off.

clue.text: Slanderous comment that stems from endless drink

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to slurp is to drink noisily, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A nasty remark made under the influence of too much alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at drunken words, and slurred speech fits it too. 'Drink' is the verb, a noisy one: to slurp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insinuation or insult that damages someone's reputation, a defamatory remark.

clue.text: Come to fair

blocks.note: a verb for a sum amounting to a total
fair in the sense of even-handed, the adjective

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to' looks like 'wake up' or 'attend', and 'fair' like a funfair; the verb sense is a sum amounting to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Two plus two comes to four, it amounts to it; fair shares are even ones, with no side getting more.

clue.text: Flyer admits family to chopper that arrives early

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a moth is a flying insect
ilk means kind or family
used as it stands

explanation.surface: An airline lets a family board a helicopter that has turned up ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' is both a helicopter, which the surface wants, and slang for a tooth. The one that arrives early is a baby's first tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's first teeth, which later fall out, are called milk teeth, and choppers is slang for teeth.

clue.text: Accountant finally gets raise, holding certain financial position

indicators.note: what comes finally comes last, so only the closing letter is kept
to hold something is to have it within your grasp

blocks.note: the last letter of accountant
to rear children is to raise them
sure = certain

explanation.surface: An accountant finally gets a pay rise, putting them in a secure financial position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' is set up as a pay rise, and is the verb to rear. The definition is a job title: a position someone holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer who manages the money of a club, company or government, a job in finance.

clue.text: Group of musicians taking back half of joint

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: in carpentry a tenon slots into a mortise, one of the two halves of that joint

explanation.surface: A band sending back half of their shared marijuana cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of joint' looks like a deletion instruction, but it is a description: the tenon is half of a mortise-and-tenon joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine players, as a quartet is four and a quintet is five.
